chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Whoever embraces Islam while an inheritance is still undivided, he is entitled to his share of the inheritance; and if he embraces Islam after the inheritance has been divided, he has no share in it."
ai.seo_question: Does a convert to Islam inherit from a relative who died before their conversion?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the timing of inheritance eligibility for new converts, distinguishing between pre-distribution and post-distribution conversion. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the right to inherit is fixed at the moment of death, provided the convert is alive and has not been excluded by other legal barriers, emphasizing the importance of the estate division process in determining final entitlements.
